name: PD 174 was established by Ordinance No. 18230, passed by the Dallas City Council on April 18, 1984. Ordinance No. 18230 amended Ordinance No. 10962, Chapter 51 of the Dallas City Code, as amended. Subsequently, Ordinance No. 18230 was amended by Ordinance No. 22956, passed by the Dallas City Council on November 13, 1996, and Ordinance No. 24101, passed by the Dallas City Council on November 10, 1999. (Ord. Nos. 10962; 18230; 22956; 24101; 25508; 26296)
source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 174 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text: SEC. 51P-174.101.LEGISLATIVE HISTORY. PD 174 was established by Ordinance No. 18230, passed by the Dallas City Council on April 18, 1984. Ordinance No. 18230 amended Ordinance No. 10962, Chapter 51 of the Dallas City Code, as amended. Subsequently, Ordinance No. 18230 was amended by Ordinance No. 22956, passed by the Dallas City Council on November 13, 1996, and Ordinance No. 24101, passed by the Dallas City Council on November 10, 1999. (Ord. Nos. 10962; 18230; 22956; 24101; 25508; 26296)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text: SEC. 51P-174.102.PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE. PD 174 is established on property generally located at the west corner of Lemmon Avenue and Carlisle Street. The size of PD 174 is approximately 3.28 acres. (Ord. Nos. 18230; 25508; 26296)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-174.103.DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.
(a)Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations contained in Chapter 51 apply. In this article: PARKWAY means that portion of a street right-of-way between the projected street curb and the lot line of the Property.
(b)Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.
(c)This district is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district.
(d)Phase 1 and Phase 2 are those areas shown on the conceptual plan. (Ord. Nos. 22956; 25508; 26296)

sections.title: Conceptual Plan
sections.text: SEC. 51P-174.104.CONCEPTUAL PLAN. Development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan (174A). In the event of a conflict between the text of this article and the conceptual plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. Nos. 22956; 24101; 25508; 26296)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text: SEC. 51P-174.105.DEVELOPMENT PLAN. A development plan must be approved by the city plan commission before issuance of any building permit. Development and use of the Property must comply with the approved development plan. The development plan and any amendments must comply with the conceptual plan and this article. (Ord. Nos. 22956; 24101; 25508; 26296)

sections.title: Uses
sections.text: SEC. 51P-174.106.USES. The only main uses permitted in this district are multiple-family with accessory private swimming pool, game court center, private recreation club or area, private club, medical clinic or ambulatory surgical center, optical shop, medical appliance fitting and sales, electrical substation, local utilities, restaurant without drive-in service, all professional, personal service, and custom crafts uses (see Section 51-4.210) except taxidermist and commercial wedding chapel, and all retail uses (see Section 51- 4.211) except feed store, second hand store, pawn shop, home improvement center, and swimming pool sale and supply. (Ord. Nos. 24101; 25508; 26296)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-174.107.YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.
(a)Setbacks.
(1)Phase 1.
(A)Minimum setback from Lemmon Avenue is 20 feet.
(B)Minimum setback from Carlisle Place is 20 feet.
(C)Minimum setback from the Katy Trail is 15 feet.
(D)No setback is required from the phase line shown on the conceptual plan.
(2)Phase 2.
(A)Minimum setback from Lemmon Avenue is 10 feet, and maximum setback from Lemmon Avenue is 65 feet.
(B)Minimum setback from Carlisle Street is 15 feet, and maximum setback from Carlisle Street is 25 feet.
(C)Minimum setback from Carlisle Place is 15 feet.
(D)No setback is required from the phase line shown on the conceptual plan.
(E)Buildings facing Carlisle Street and Lemmon Avenue, having a setback greater than the required minimum setback as set forth in this paragraph, must have a facade located between the maximum and the minimum setbacks for at least 70 percent of the linear distance of the street frontage exclusive of each of the following:
(i)private streets, drives, or pedestrian ways;
(ii)any pedestrian plaza having a maximum depth of 50 feet (measured from the building frontage to the street) and a maximum length of 20 percent of the length of the building frontage; or
(iii)for corner lots, the depth of the maximum setback from the perpendicular street frontage of that lot.
(3)Exception for projections. Canopies, balconies, stoops, bay windows, awnings, other ordinary building projections, street furniture, planting beds, and outdoor eating areas may extend into a setback provided that a minimum horizontal sidewalk clearance of six feet and a minimum vertical clearance for any building projections of ten feet is maintained.
(4)Exception for structures other than the buildings. There is no minimum setback for structures other than buildings.
(b)Dwelling unit density. Maximum number of dwelling units is 260.
(c)Floor area. Maximum floor area is a total of 355,000 square feet of which a maximum of 350,000 square feet is permitted on Phase 2. Non-residential uses shall not exceed 40,000 square feet of which a maximum of 35,000 square feet is permitted on Phase 2.
(d)Height. Maximum structure height is 180 feet for Phase 1 and 85 feet for Phase 2, exclusive of roof top mechanicals, parapet walls, and elevator penthouses which may be 12 feet higher.
(e)Maximum lot coverage is 80 percent. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.
(f)Lot size. No minimum lot size.
(g)Stories. No maximum number of stories. (Ord. Nos. 22956; 25508; 26296)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-174.108.OFF-STREET PARKING.
(a)In general. The off-street parking requirements of Section 51P-193.107 and Section 51P-193.113 and the off-street loading regulations of 51P-193.115 apply, except as otherwise provided in this section.
(b)Non-residential uses in Phase 2. In Phase 2, if more than four pedestrian amenities listed in Section 51P-174.110(g) are provided, non-residential uses shall be granted reductions of four percent of total parking requirements for each additional pedestrian amenity up to a maximum 20 percent reduction. If a reduction in parking requirements is sought, bicycle parking must be provided as an amenity type. The additional pedestrian amenities must be provided within the curb-to-building area or in a pedestrian plaza and must serve to enhance pedestrian pathways from building entrances to trolley or transit stops. The amenities may also be provided in any area containing private streets or drives and their pedestrian ways.
(c)On-street parking. On-street parallel or head-in parking spaces located on Carlisle Street or Carlisle Place or any private street or drive on or adjacent to the Property may be counted toward the off-street parking requirements based on the following: 50 percent of the parking spaces located on Carlisle Place; 100 percent of the parking spaces located on any private street or drive on or adjacent to the Property and 100 percent of the Carlisle Street parallel parking spaces. This subsection does not abrogate the authority of the city's traffic engineer to regulate traffic, including parking on public streets.
(d)Shared parking. Total required parking may be adjusted pursuant to the mixed use development (MUD) parking chart provided in Section 51P-193.113(g)(4) (Exhibit 193F). Up to 20 percent of parking for residential uses may be used as non-residential parking between 7:30 a.m. and 6:30 p.m.
(e)Loading. Only one loading space is required. The required loading space must be either a medium or large space as described in Section 51P-193.115. (Ord. Nos. 22956; 25508; 26296)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text: SEC. 51P-174.109.ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS. See Article VI. (Ord. 26296)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-174.110.LANDSCAPING.
(a)In general. Landscaping must be provided in accordance with the requirements of Section 51P-193.126, with this district considered to be a GR subdistrict for landscape requirements, except that if off-street parking is reduced pursuant to Section 51P-174.108(b), landscaping must be provided in accordance with the special landscape and open space provisions in Subsection (g).
(b)Installation date. Landscaping must be installed within six months after the issuance of a certificate of occupancy.
(c)Sidewalks. Sidewalks along Lemmon Avenue, Carlisle Street, and Carlisle Place must have a minimum width of eight feet, and a minimum unobstructed width of six feet.
(d)Private license granted.
(1)The city council hereby grants a revocable, non-exclusive license to the owners, or with the written consent of the owner, to the tenants ("property owner") of all property in this district for the exclusive purpose of authorizing compliance with the parkway landscaping requirements of this article. A property owner is not required to pay an initial or annual fee for this license, although a fee may be charged for issuance of a parkway landscape permit in accordance with the Dallas Building Code or Subsection (e) of this section. This private license shall not terminate at the end of any specific time period, however, the city council reserves and has the absolute right to terminate this license at will, by resolution passed by the city council, any time such termination becomes necessary. The determination by the city of the necessity for such termination shall be final and binding and the city shall become entitled to possession of the premises without giving any notice and without the necessity of legal proceedings to obtain possession whenever in its judgment the purpose or use of this license is inconsistent with the public use of the right-of-way or when the purpose or use of this license is likely to become a nuisance or a public safety issue. Upon termination of the license by the director, each property owner shall remove all improvements and installations in the public rights-of-way in a manner satisfactory to the director of public works and transportation.
(2)A property owner is not required to comply with any landscaping requirement if compliance is made impossible due to the director's revocation of a landscape permit or the revocation of the license granted herein affecting landscaping.
(3)Upon the installation of landscaping and related amenities, such as irrigation systems, in the public rights-of-way, the property owner shall procure, pay for and keep in full force and effect commercial general liability insurance coverage with an insurance company authorized to do business in the State of Texas and otherwise acceptable to the city, covering, but not limited to, the liability assumed under the license granted herein, with combined single limits of liability for bodily injury and property damage of not less that $1,000,000 for each occurrence, $2,000,000 annual aggregate. Coverage under this liability policy shall be on an "occurrence" basis and the city shall be named as additional insured. Proof of such insurance shall be sent to: Office of Risk Management, City of Dallas, 1500 Marilla, l/C/North; Dallas, Texas 75201 and the policy shall provide for 30 days prior written notice to the Office of Risk Management of cancellation, expiration, non-renewal, or material change in coverage. All subrogation rights for loss or damage against the city are hereby waived to the extent it is covered by this liability insurance policy.
(4)Each property owner shall be responsible for maintaining the landscaping and related amenities in good repair and condition and to keep the premises safe and from deteriorating in value or condition, at no expense to the city, and the city shall be absolutely exempt from any requirements to make repairs or to maintain the landscaping and related amenities. The granting of a license for landscaping and related amenities under this section does not release the property owner from liability in the installation or maintenance of trees, landscaping, and related amenities in the public right- of-way.
(e)Parkway landscape permit.
(1)It is the responsibility of the property owner to apply for and obtain a parkway landscape permit before locating trees, landscaping, or related amenities in the parkway. An application for a parkway landscape permit must be made to the director of public works and transportation before an application for a building permit is made for work on the lot. The application must be in writing on a form approved by the director and accompanied by plans or drawings showing the area of the parkway affected and the planting or other amenities proposed.
(2)Upon receipt of the application and any required fees, the director shall circulate it to an affected city departments and utilities for review and comment. If, after receiving comments from affected city departments and utilities, the director determines that the construction and planting or other amenities proposed will not be inconsistent with and will not unreasonably impair the public use of the right-of-way, the director shall issue a parkway landscape permit to the property owner; otherwise, the director shall deny the permit.
(3)A property owner is not required to comply with any parkway landscaping requirement of this article if compliance is made impossible due to the director's denial of a parkway landscape permit.
(4)A parkway landscape permit issued by the director is subject to immediate revocation upon written notice if at any time the director determines that the use of the parkway authorized by the permit is inconsistent with or unreasonably impairs the public use of the right-of-way. The property owner is not required to comply with any parkway landscaping requirement of this section if compliance is made impossible due to the director's revocation of a parkway landscape permit.
(f)Pedestrian amenities for reduced parking for lots in Phase 2.
(1)Bicycle parking at one 5-bicycle unit per 100 feet of frontage, with a minimum of two per lot is required.
(2)The following pedestrian amenities must be provided within the curb-to-building area of the lot:
(A)Awnings/canopies with a minimum overhang of four feet and a minimum length of 25 feet per 100 feet of building facade along the frontage; or a combination of street trees and evergreen shrubs with a minimum of one small tree per 25 feet of frontage and a minimum of one shrub per five feet of frontage.
(B)Benches at one per 100 feet of frontage, with a minimum of two per lot.
(C)Trash receptacles at one per 100 feet of frontage, with a minimum of two per lot.
(D)Pedestrian street lamps (free-standing or wall-mounted) at one per 50 feet of frontage.
(E)Enhanced sidewalk with stamped concrete or brick pavers for the full width of the sidewalk along the entire frontage.
(F)Public art or water features costing no less than $2,500, at one per lot.
(G)Drinking fountains at one per lot.
(3)Amenities must be placed far enough from the street curb so as not to create a physical barrier to buses.
(4)Canopies, awnings, and pedestrian street lamp fixtures must have a minimum nine-foot clearance. Lamp fixtures may not exceed 14 feet in height. Light fixtures may not emit light upward into the windows of dwelling units.
(5)All pedestrian amenities must be maintained by the owner of the lot; if there is more than one owner, all owners are jointly and severally liable for maintenance.
(g)Special landscape and open space provisions.
(1)Parking lot screening. A five-foot-wide landscaped strip must be located along any edge of a parking lot or parking structure that is visible at grade level from a street or alley, in accordance with the following provisions:
(A)Small trees must be located every 15 feet, or fraction thereof, or clustered every 30 feet, within the landscaped strip. A small tree must have a minimum caliper of three inches, except that multi-trunk trees must have a minimum caliper of two inches per trunk.
(B)A continuous row of large evergreen shrubs must be located in the landscaped strip.
(C)For every four rows of parking, parking lots must contain at least one interior landscaped strip of at least 15 linear feet that is planted with ground cover, shrubbery of 24 to 36 inches in height, and at least one large tree.
(D)Fences may complement but not substitute for parking lot trees and shrubbery screening.
(E)Covered parking may substitute for trees and shrubbery in the interior of the parking area, but not along its perimeter. Covered parking may not replace shrubbery or substitute for trees that provide buffering between parking lots or parking structures and the street.
(2)Screening of off-street loading spaces.
(A)All off-street loading spaces must be screened from all public streets adjacent to the lot.
(B)Screening of all off-street loading spaces must be at least six feet high.
(C)Garbage storage areas must be visually screened on all sides by a brick, stone, or concrete masonry, stucco, concrete, or wood wall or fence. Screening is not required on a side adjacent to an alley or easement used for garbage pick-up service. Trellises or other coverings must be used to screen the top of garbage storage areas.
(3)Street trees. A small street tree must be provided for every 50 feet of frontage, with a minimum of two trees per lot. A small tree must have a minimum caliper of three inches, except that multi-trunk trees must have a minimum caliper of two inches per trunk. Street trees must be located within five feet of the street curb. If the buffer zone is located in the public right-of-way, street trees must be located in the public right-of way.
(4)Tree grates. Any tree within 18 inches of a curb must be protected by a tree grate.
(5)Permeable surface area. A minimum of 10 percent of the Property area must be open space in the form of permeable surfaces such as perimeter landscape buffer strip, recreation area, conservation area, or crushed gravel. Discrete open space areas smaller than 25 square feet or less than five feet wide and landscaping in the public right-of-way are not counted towards this 10 percent requirement. (Ord. Nos. 22956; 25508; 26296)

sections.title: Signs Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-174.111.SIGNS REGULATIONS.
(a)Except as otherwise provided in this section, signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts in Article VII.
(b)The following modifications to Article VII sign regulations for non-business zoning districts apply in Phase 2.
(1)Detached signs are prohibited except for directional signs.
(2)Signs must be premise signs or convey a noncommercial message.
(3)The maximum number of signs is two per facade per occupant of the premise in addition to blade signs.
(4)Words consisting of characters less than four inches high may be used without limit, and shall not be considered in computing the effective area.
(5)Individual signs may not have more than eight words consisting of characters in excess of four inches in height.
(6)The maximum effective area of signs is 40 square feet except that signs for non- residential uses on the ground floor may not exceed three feet in height and may not exceed 38 square feet or 75 percent of the length of the facade of the premise of the advertiser, whichever is greater. Signs for non-residential uses on the ground floor may not have moving or flashing parts and may not have illumination exceeding 200 foot lamberts.
(7)Signs must be mounted parallel to the building surface except blade signs.
(8)Signs may not project more than 18 inches from the surface to which they are attached, except that one blade sign is permitted to be attached to the Lemmon Avenue facade of a building, one blade sign is permitted to be attached to the Carlisle Street facade of the building and one blade sign is permitted to be attached to the comer of the building at the intersection of Lemmon Avenue and Carlisle Street. Blade signs may not exceed 60 square feet in effective area per side, may project up to four feet from the surface of the building, may not project above the roof of the facade to which it is attached, must be at least 10 feet above grade, and may be illuminated up to 200 foot lamberts. For purposes of this provision, blade sign means a sign projecting perpendicularly from the building facade, or if at a building corner at an angle of 135 degrees.
(9)Signs may not be mounted on roofs.
(10)Signs may not project above roofs.
(11)Signs for non-residential uses, other than the blade signs, are not permitted above the ground floor of the building.
(12)Temporary sandwich board signs, not to exceed 12 square feet of effective area per side, are permitted to be placed on the sidewalks. Sandwich board signs may only advertise uses located within the property and must comply with the requirements for minimum sidewalk clearance. Sandwich board signs must comply with the visibility triangle provisions contained in Section 51P- 193.104(a)(46). (Ord. Nos. 22956; 25508; 26296)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-174.112.ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.
(a)The entire Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.
(b)Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 22956; 25508; 26102; 26296)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-174.113.COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.
(a)All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation.
(b)The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use in this district until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 24101; 25508; 26102; 26296)

sections.title: Zoning Map
sections.text: SEC. 51P-174.114.ZONING MAP. PD 174 is located on Zoning Map No. I-7. (Ord. Nos. 18230; 25508; 26296)
